title: Popcorn hexagon
subtitle: One popcorn at each of the six corner points — a raised dot visible from across the room
excerpt: The popcorn hexagon puts one popcorn stitch at each of its six corner points, surrounded by trebles in each round. The popcorn stands out on the public face — a raised dome at every corner that reads clearly even in a single colour and from a distance.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — raised-stitch hexagonal motifs (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet motif chapter.
heroPrompt: A popcorn crochet hexagon in deep rose DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight — the 12 cm motif shows six pronounced raised popcorn domes at the corner points against a background of flat trebles.

chartDefinition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. One popcorn sits at each of the six corner points on every round, flanked by chain-2 spaces. Trebles fill the side spaces between corners from round 2.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five (or more) trebles worked into the same stitch or space, the hook removed and reinserted through the top of the first treble and the last loop, then pulled through to close. The result is a rounded raised dome, different from a cluster in that the stitches stand separately before being gathered.
The gap created by skipping a chain or chains. In the popcorn hexagon, a chain-2 space flanks each popcorn corner; chain-1 spaces sit between side groups.

content.text: The popcorn hexagon places one
popcorn

stitch at the centre of each of its six corner points, flanked by chain-2 spaces and surrounded by flat trebles in each round. The popcorn stands out on the public face as a rounded raised dome — a different texture from a cluster because the individual trebles are visible before they are gathered, giving a more three-dimensional point.
Each
chain-space

flanking the popcorn keeps the corners open so the motif lies flat. The popcorn needs a slightly looser tension than average to sit fully rounded — if yours are pulling flat, work the five trebles of the popcorn slightly looser before closing.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins — the popcorn domes need gentle steam rather than heavy pressing to stay rounded.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished four-round popcorn hexagon measures 12 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking. Popcorns affect sizing more than standard clusters; swatch one motif before starting a project.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
popcorn (pc) — 5 tr into the same space, hook removed and reinserted through the first tr, pulled through to close. UK and US technique is the same; only the component stitch name differs.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Ch 3 at the start of each round does not count as a stitch — it lifts the yarn to working height before the first popcorn or treble. Do not turn.
How to work a popcorn (pc)

Work 5 tr into the same space. Remove the hook from the last loop. Insert the hook from front to back through the top of the first of the 5 tr. Pick up the dropped loop. Pull it through to close the popcorn. Ch 1 to secure.
Round 1

Form a magic ring. Ch 3. Work a pc into the ring. *Ch 2, work a pc into the ring*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st into top of first pc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 popcorns, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 2

Sl st into first ch-2 sp. Ch 3. Work 2 tr into same sp. Work a pc into same sp. Work 2 tr into same sp. *Ch 2. Into next ch-2 sp work (2 tr, pc, 2 tr)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st into top of first tr to join. (6 popcorns flanked by 2 tr each side, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 3

Sl st into first ch-2 sp. Ch 3. Work 2 tr into same sp. Work a pc into same sp. Work 2 tr into same sp. Ch 1. *Into the gap between corner groups work 3 tr. Ch 1. Into next ch-2 sp work (2 tr, pc, 2 tr). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Into the gap work 3 tr. Ch 1. Sl st to top of first tr to join. (6 popcorn corners, 6 side clusters of 3 tr, 6 ch-2 spaces, 12 ch-1 side spaces.)
Round 4

Sl st into first ch-2 sp. Ch 3. Work 2 tr into same sp. Work a pc into same sp. Work 2 tr into same sp. Ch 1. *[Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Into next ch-2 sp work (2 tr, pc, 2 tr). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. [Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Sl st to top of first tr to join. Fasten off. (6 popcorn corners, 12 side clusters, 6 ch-2 spaces, 18 ch-1 side spaces.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Popcorns mark the six corners on every round; three-treble side groups fill the edges from round 3.

definition.title: Popcorn hexagon
definition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. One popcorn at each of the six corners throughout, flanked by chain-2 spaces. Three-treble side groups fill the edges from round 3.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail. Steam-block on a foam mat with all six corner points pinned. Hold the steam iron 3 to 4 cm above the surface rather than pressing down — popcorns collapse under direct pressing and do not recover.
Joining

Join along each of the six sides through the back loops of the side treble groups, matching side clusters edge to edge. The popcorn corners sit slightly proud of the join seam — this is correct. For a join-as-you-go method, work round 4 normally on the first hexagon, then on each subsequent hexagon replace the shared-side chain-1 spaces with a sl st into the corresponding chain-1 space of the adjacent motif.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. The popcorn domes may flatten slightly in the wash — re-steam gently while damp and allow to dry flat without pressing. Do not tumble-dry.
What to try next

The treble cluster hexagon uses a similar raised corner technique but works a 5-tr cluster rather than a popcorn, giving a slightly flatter tip. The lacy hexagon moves in the opposite direction — open chain-3 side spaces for an airy finish suited to shawls and lightweight panels.
